name: Alexandria
tagline: Egypt's Mediterranean second city, founded by Alexander the Great, where ancient catacombs sit beneath a modern seafront.
highlight: Standing on the ramparts of Qaitbay Citadel, built from the fallen stones of the ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria, waves from the same Mediterranean crashing below.
shortDescription: Egypt's Mediterranean second city, founded by Alexander the Great, home to a striking modern library, ancient catacombs and a long seafront corniche.
metaDescription: An Alexandria travel guide: the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, Qaitbay Citadel, the catacombs, food and how to plan a visit to Egypt's coastal city.
nearestAirport: Borg El Arab Airport (HBE), or via Cairo
knownFor: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina, Qaitbay Citadel, Mediterranean seafood
goodFor: History, coastal walks, a change of pace from the Nile

image.alt: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina, Alexandria's striking modern library

intro: Alexandria is Egypt's Mediterranean second city, founded by Alexander the Great in 331 BCE and once home to the ancient world's greatest library and one of its Seven Wonders, the Lighthouse of Alexandria.

That ancient legacy lives on in a striking modern form, the Bibliotheca Alexandrina rising directly on the shore as a deliberate tribute to its lost predecessor, alongside genuine Roman-era catacombs still being explored.

Most visitors treat it as a refreshing change of pace from the Nile Valley's desert heat, a breezy seafront city with its own long corniche, seafood restaurants and a noticeably more relaxed, cosmopolitan character.

whyVisit.intro: Alexandria's case rests on combining a legendary ancient legacy with a relaxed Mediterranean coastal character.

points.title: It's a refreshing change of pace from the Nile Valley

attractionsIntro: Alexandria's essential sights combine legendary ancient history with a relaxed Mediterranean seafront.

attractions.name: The Bibliotheca Alexandrina
attractions.text: A striking modern library built as a deliberate tribute to the legendary ancient Library of Alexandria, lost to history.
attractions.tip: The building's sloped, disc-shaped design is meant to evoke a rising sun over the Mediterranean.

attractions.name: Qaitbay Citadel
attractions.text: Built from the fallen stones of the ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
attractions.tip: The citadel's ramparts offer sweeping views back along Alexandria's curving harbour.

attractions.name: Alexandria's corniche

image.file: File:Egypt, Alexandria, The Corniche of Alexandria, Mediterranean Sea.jpg
image.alt: Alexandria's seafront corniche along the Mediterranean

attractions.text: A long, breezy seafront promenade, curving along the harbour past cafés, fishermen and the citadel itself.
attractions.tip: A sunset walk here is one of Alexandria's best free experiences.

attractions.name: The Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa

image.file: File:Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, Alexandria, Egypt.jpg
image.alt: The Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa in Alexandria

attractions.text: A fascinating Roman-era burial site, its carvings blending Egyptian, Greek and Roman styles in a single place.
attractions.tip: One of the largest known Roman-era burial sites in Egypt, worth a proper guided visit.

attractions.name: Pompey's Pillar

image.file: File:Pompey's Pillar (Archaeological site in Alexandria 2017) , photo by Hatem moushir 9.jpg

attractions.text: A towering Roman-era granite column, despite its name actually unrelated to the historical figure Pompey.
attractions.tip: Combine with the nearby Serapeum ruins, part of the same archaeological site.

attractions.name: Montaza Palace

image.file: File:Montaza Palace, Alexandria, Egypt - Murat Özsoy 2018.jpg
image.alt: Montaza Palace and its gardens in Alexandria

attractions.text: A beautiful former royal palace, its gardens and seafront setting now open as a public park.
attractions.tip: A peaceful spot for a walk, with real views over the Mediterranean from the palace grounds.

attractions.name: The view from Qaitbay Citadel

image.file: File:A view of Alexandria from the Citadel of Qaitbay.jpg

attractions.text: One of the city's best views, the full sweep of Alexandria's harbour and corniche visible from the ramparts.
attractions.tip: Visit in late afternoon for the most flattering light over the water.

thingsToDoIntro: Alexandria rewards a relaxed pace, mixing ancient history with real time along the Mediterranean.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Bibliotheca Alexandrina
thingsToDo.text: An absorbing few hours, taking in the library's striking architecture and attached museums.
thingsToDo.tip: The antiquities museum within the complex is easy to miss but well worth the extra time.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Qaitbay Citadel's ramparts
thingsToDo.text: A worthwhile hour, exploring the fortress built from the ancient lighthouse's own fallen stones.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine with a corniche walk, since the citadel sits right at its western end.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the corniche at sunset

image.file: File:Egypt, Alexandria, The Corniche of Alexandria.jpg

thingsToDo.text: An essential Alexandria evening, strolling the long seafront promenade as the light fades over the water.
thingsToDo.tip: A good spot to find fresh seafood dinner afterward.

thingsToDo.title: Descend into the Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa

image.file: File:Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa, Alexandria, Egypt - 50852603056.jpg
image.alt: Descending into the Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa

thingsToDo.text: A fascinating underground visit, tracing a unique blend of Egyptian, Greek and Roman burial traditions.
thingsToDo.tip: A guide adds real context to the mix of cultural influences carved into the walls.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Pompey's Pillar

image.file: File:Pompey's Pillar (Archaeological site in Alexandria in 2017) , photo by Hatem Moushir 39.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A quick, worthwhile stop, standing beneath one of Alexandria's few remaining ancient monuments above ground.
thingsToDo.tip: Combine with the Catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa, since both sit relatively close together.

thingsToDo.title: Relax in Montaza Palace's gardens

image.file: File:MONTAZA GARDENS AND PARK, ALEXANDRIA, EGYPT.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A peaceful escape from the city centre, walking former royal gardens overlooking the Mediterranean.
thingsToDo.tip: A good spot for a relaxed afternoon away from the busier central sights.

foodIntro: Alexandria's food leans on fresh Mediterranean seafood, a real change from the Nile Valley's traditional staples.

foods.name: Fresh Mediterranean seafood
foods.text: Some of Egypt's best, grilled or fried fish and shellfish landed straight from the Mediterranean.

foods.name: Koshari

image.alt: Koshari, Egypt's national dish of rice, lentils and pasta

foods.text: A reliable classic, found throughout the city at every price point.

foods.name: Ful medames

image.alt: Ful medames, a traditional Egyptian fava bean breakfast

foods.text: An essential breakfast, found at cafés throughout the city.
foods.whereToTry: Breakfast stalls and cafés throughout Alexandria.

foods.name: Taameya (Egyptian falafel)
foods.text: Egypt's own fava bean version of falafel, a beloved local street food.

foods.name: Molokhia
foods.text: A beloved home-style dish, often made here with a seafood variation given the coastal setting.

foods.name: Karkade (hibiscus tea)
foods.text: A refreshing national drink, well suited to Alexandria's Mediterranean breeze.
foods.whereToTry: Cafés and restaurants throughout the city.

gettingThere.intro: Alexandria is well connected to Cairo, making it an easy addition to a wider Egypt itinerary.

options.text: Fast and comfortable, taking around two and a half to three hours.
options.detail: Frequent daily departures make this the most popular way to travel between the two cities.

options.text: A budget-friendly alternative to the train, similar in duration.
options.detail: Regular services run throughout the day.

options.mode: Flight to Borg El Arab Airport
options.text: A faster option for those short on time.
options.detail: The airport sits a bit outside the city centre, requiring an onward taxi.

gettingAround.intro: Alexandria's long corniche layout makes taxis useful for longer distances, though the centre itself is walkable.

options.text: Pleasant for the central stretch between the citadel and library.
options.detail: The corniche's full length is long — a taxi helps for the far ends.

options.text: Useful for reaching Montaza Palace and the catacombs.
options.detail: Widely available and inexpensive throughout the city.

options.text: A characterful, budget-friendly way to see parts of the city.
options.detail: One of the oldest tram networks in Africa, still running today.

bestTime.headline: April to June and September to November for the most pleasant Mediterranean weather
bestTime.summary: Alexandria's Mediterranean climate is milder than the Nile Valley, making it comfortable across a wider range of seasons.

seasons.text: The most pleasant weather, warm without the intense heat of Egypt's interior.
Warm and busy with domestic tourists escaping Cairo's heat, though the sea breeze keeps it comfortable.
Cooler and rainier than the rest of Egypt, Alexandria's most distinctly Mediterranean season.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Alexandria's milder coastal climate makes it workable across most of the year.

itinerary.intro: Built around the Bibliotheca Alexandrina and the citadel on day one, ancient sites on day two.

days.evening: A sunset walk along the corniche.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make an Alexandria visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Take the train from Cairo — it's fast, comfortable and the most popular way to travel.
Bring a light jacket, even in warmer months — Alexandria's sea breeze is often cooler than inland Egypt.
Book Bibliotheca Alexandrina tickets ahead if visiting during a busy period.
Try the fresh seafood along the corniche — it's a real highlight of visiting.
Combine Pompey's Pillar and the catacombs in one trip, given their proximity.
Consider Alexandria as a day trip from Cairo if short on time elsewhere in Egypt.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Alexandria?
faq.a: Two days covers the Bibliotheca Alexandrina, Qaitbay Citadel and the main ancient sites comfortably.

faq.q: Can you visit Alexandria as a day trip from Cairo?
faq.a: Yes — the train takes under three hours each way, making it a workable, if full, day trip.

faq.q: Is the original Library of Alexandria still standing?
faq.a: No, lost to history — the modern Bibliotheca Alexandrina was built nearby as a deliberate tribute to it.
Its Mediterranean seafront setting, ancient history founded by Alexander the Great, and a striking modern library built in tribute to its lost predecessor.

faq.q: Is Alexandria warmer or cooler than Cairo?
faq.a: Cooler, thanks to its Mediterranean coastal position and sea breeze, a welcome contrast to inland Egypt's desert heat.

faq.q: Is Qaitbay Citadel really built on the site of an Ancient Wonder?
faq.a: Yes — it stands on the site of, and partly built from, the fallen stones of the ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria.
